title: HORMUZ GATE — Red / Blue / Purple CTF Overlay
rules_of_engagement: No live packets leave the sim. All AIS/GNSS/ICS nodes are sandboxed twins.
Red may RECON, CLASSIFY, and REPORT. Red may not be given recipes to jam GNSS, spoof AIS, or operate OT against real plants.
Blue defends: detect anomaly class, isolate twin, restore integrity, write the after-action.
Purple owns the detection spine and scores both sides on evidence quality.
Dubai Marina track is a LEGAL INVESTIGATION, not a flight-authorization bypass.

RED.name: SPECTER RECON
RED.mission: Map the twin. Identify which anomaly class is present. Capture recon flags by answering detection quizzes at each pin.

BLUE.name: HORMUZ WATCH
BLUE.mission: Detect, contain, restore the twin. Capture defense flags by choosing the correct control (NIST 800-82 / IMO cyber / GCAA).

PURPLE.name: ATHELGARD RANGE
PURPLE.mission: Score evidence. Confirm flags only when the learner cites a public class (jamming vs spoofing vs dark AIS vs legal no-fly), not a method.

spawn.label: Jebel Ali outer harbor holding pattern

tracks.name: Strait of Hormuz Cyber Threats
tracks.brief: The twin replays publicly reported 2025–2026 Gulf GNSS/AIS disruption CLASSES: jamming (signal denied), spoofing (false but coherent fix), crop-circle AIS clusters over land/airports, dark-AIS gaps, destination-field distress text. Learners classify and defend. They do not operate a jammer.

tracks.name: Dubai Marina Drone-Law Investigation
tracks.brief: A tourist FPV clip was uploaded tagged Dubai Marina at night. Investigate whether the flight was lawful under GCAA + DCAA, and what control the operator missed. Outcome is a legal finding, not a permit.

tracks.name: NIST SP 800-82r3 OT Segmentation
tracks.brief: Sandbox export-terminal twin taught against NIST SP 800-82 Revision 3 (Sept 2023), Guide to Operational Technology Security. r3 expands ICS→OT, aligns to CSF and 800-53r5 OT overlay (low/mod/high baselines), and treats segmentation as zones + controlled conduits — Purdue as vocabulary, IEC 62443 as zone/conduit enforcement language. No live plant, no protocol exploits.

tracks.name: IEC 62443-3-2 Zone Design
tracks.brief: Zone design is IEC 62443-3-2 (2020): define the System Under Consideration, partition into zones and conduits, assess risk per zone/conduit, assign target Security Level SL-T, document requirements. 62443-3-3 then states the system requirements for that SL. Purdue labels function; 62443 zones are drawn by shared security requirement and risk.

tracks.name: NIST SP 800-53r5 OT Overlay Review
tracks.brief: The OT overlay lives in NIST SP 800-82r3 Appendix F. It is a partial tailoring of 800-53 Rev. 5 / 800-53B Low-Moderate-High baselines plus OT Discussion text. Overlay reference name: NIST SP 800-82 Rev 3 Operational Technology Overlay. Compensating controls (PL-11) meet intent when the device cannot host the control — not waivers. Teaching plate is schematic; official control IDs come from Appendix F.

pins.name: Hormuz Pinch — AIS Crop Circle
pins.anomaly_class: GNSS spoofing reflected in AIS (geometric cluster / land overlay)
pins.public_context: Windward / JMIC / OCCRP-class reporting in 2026 described ships painting false positions over airports, plants, and inland points; researchers call tight circular AIS blooms crop circles.

red_quiz.prompt: AIS shows 40 tankers stacked in a perfect 2 km circle over an inland airport. What CLASS is this?
choices: Normal anchorage pattern
GNSS spoofing feeding AIS (false coherent fix)
Simple radio silence / dark AIS
ECDIS chart datum mismatch only
red_quiz.teach: Jamming DENIES a fix. Spoofing REPLACES it with a convincing lie. AIS often inherits the lie, so the whole picture looks geometric and wrong.

blue_quiz.prompt: Bridge team on the twin reports GPS jumping 40 km inland. First SAFE control?
choices: Trust the new fix and speed up transit
Cross-fix with radar, visual, and terrestrial aids; treat GNSS as untrusted; log and report to UKMTO/JMIC-class desk
Disable AIS entirely for the rest of the voyage without procedure
Reboot the cargo PLC network
blue_quiz.teach: Defense is integrity of navigation, not offense against the interference source. Multi-sensor cross-fix + report is the published mariners' control.

pins.skill_card: ICS/Nav — distinguish jamming vs spoofing vs dark AIS

pins.name: Gulf of Oman Approaches — Jamming Cluster
pins.anomaly_class: GNSS jamming (loss of fix, not a coherent false position)

red_quiz.prompt: Receivers lose lock; no coherent inland teleport; many ships flicker. Class?
choices: Spoofing
Jamming / denial of GNSS
AIS identity swap (MMSI clone)
Subsea cable cut
red_quiz.teach: No lock = denial. A pretty wrong position = spoof. Do not collapse the two words.

blue_quiz.prompt: Which control belongs in the SMS when GNSS is denied in a chokepoint?
choices: Continue with last known electronic fix only
Pre-planned terrestrial / radar / visual passage plan, reduced speed, extra lookout, logged interference report
Broadcast a false AIS position to hide
Switch the engine PLC to manual and ignore the bridge
blue_quiz.teach: Published guidance treats GNSS interference as both a safety hazard and a cyber-relevant event under the Safety Management System.

pins.skill_card: Security+ / maritime — availability loss vs integrity loss

pins.name: Kharg-class Export Twin — OT Awareness
pins.anomaly_class: Exposed ICS/OT management plane on a SANDBOX twin (no live plant)

red_quiz.prompt: The twin shows a metering skid HMI reachable from a simulated business VLAN. What is the FINDING class?
choices: IT/OT zone crossing — Purdue Level mix
A valid engineering convenience
A GNSS problem
A drone-registration problem
red_quiz.teach: NIST 800-82 / IEC 62443: business networks and control networks stay segmented. The flag is the ZONE violation, not a protocol exploit.

blue_quiz.prompt: Correct Blue action on the twin?
choices: Leave the path so Red can keep scoring
Segment the OT zone, revoke the dual-homed jump, require jump-host + MFA + allow-list, preserve logs
Air-gap by yanking every cable including safety systems
Post the HMI on the public scoreboard
blue_quiz.teach: Contain + evidence. Safety instrumented systems stay up.

pins.name: Jebel Ali — Port Community System Twin
pins.anomaly_class: Supply-chain / port-community credential stuffing on a fake booking portal

red_quiz.prompt: A cloned port-community login is harvesting operator passwords. ATT&CK-class?
choices: T1078 Valid Accounts via phishing clone (credential harvest)
Physical cutting of a quay crane cable
GNSS crop circle
Legal drone overflight
red_quiz.teach: Classify the TTP. Do not run the harvest against any live portal.

choices: Ignore because it is 'just a website'
Takedown the clone, force phishing-resistant MFA, hunt reuse, notify the port SOC
Reset every crane PLC password to the same string
Ban AIS
blue_quiz.teach: Identity is the beachhead into the port community system.

pins.name: Dubai Marina — Legal Overlay
pins.anomaly_class: Unlawful recreational UAS in a restricted urban / heliport-adjacent zone
facts_learners_must_use: GCAA: register every recreational UAS; ≤5 kg recreational; green zone only via official map app; daylight; VLOS; ≤400 ft AGL; 5 km buffer from airports, airfields, heliports, HLS.
Dubai Marina sits next to Skydive Dubai airstrip / heliport — the 5 km rule paints most of the Marina red/beige without a specific authorization.
DCAA recreational rules (DCAD-RUA, 2025 directive family): Dubai requires DCAA process on top of GCAA; designated zones only; crowds/buildings standoff.
GCAA Safety Decision 2026-03 (Mar 2026) temporarily suspended UAS operations in UAE airspace unless a written exemption exists — check the CURRENT decision status inside the sim date.
Penalties in published explainers: fines, confiscation, possible custody; foreigners risk immigration action.

red_quiz.prompt: Night FPV clip geotagged Dubai Marina, 250 ft between towers, no GCAA/DCAA auth in the metadata. Lawful?
choices: Yes — Marina is a tourist green zone
No — urban towers + adjacent airfield/heliport 5 km buffer + night + likely post-2026 suspension/authorization failure
Yes if the drone weighs under 250 g
Yes if the pilot stays on a hotel balcony
red_quiz.teach: Marina is not a hobby park. Weight exemptions do not punch through airport/heliport buffers or night rules.

choices: A flight plan that sneaks the same route at dawn
A finding: zone color, nearest HLS/airfield, time-of-day, registration status, current GCAA safety decision, recommended referral to GCAA/DCAA — no flight
A patched GNSS spoof against DXB radar
A public doxx of the uploader
blue_quiz.teach: This track trains compliance investigation. The win is a clean legal brief, not a lofted quad.

pins.skill_card: GCAA CAR-UAR + DCAA DCAD-RUA + Safety Decision 2026-03 awareness

red_quiz.prompt: What published GCAA geometric control bars most of coastal Dubai for hobby UAS?
choices: 1 km from any mall
5 km from airport outer fence, heliports, HLS, airfields, plus controlled-zone maps
Only runways themselves
Nothing if you fly under 50 ft
red_quiz.teach: Memorize the 5 km published buffer. Height does not cancel it.

blue_quiz.prompt: Correct app/source of truth for 'where can I fly today'?
choices: A random YouTube 'hidden spots' video
Official GCAA / DCAA map + current Safety Decision + per-flight authorization where required
OpenStreetMap no-fly layer only
The hotel concierge
blue_quiz.teach: The map app and the live safety decision beat influencer overlays.

pins.name: Export Twin — Industrial DMZ (L3.5)
pins.anomaly_class: Missing industrial DMZ: enterprise historian client talks straight to L2 HMI

red_quiz.prompt: Enterprise BI pulls tags straight from the area HMI. Which 800-82 / Purdue control is missing?
choices: A bigger antivirus license on the HMI
An industrial DMZ (L3.5) broker — jump host / replica historian / brokered remote access — so L4/L5 never touch L2/L1
Turning off all safety instrumented systems
Publishing the HMI to the internet with TLS
red_quiz.teach: 800-82r3: OT and enterprise stay separated. Traffic crosses through DMZ services, not a flat cable. L3.5 is industry shorthand, not an ISA-95 number.

blue_quiz.prompt: Correct Blue restore on the twin?
choices: NAT the HMI onto the corporate Wi-Fi
Stand up L3.5: replica historian facing IT, jump host + MFA for engineering, default-deny conduit, logs kept
Air-gap by pulling the SIS too
Move the PLC onto the same VLAN as email
blue_quiz.teach: Broker the conduit. Do not flatten the plant to make the dashboard easier.

pins.name: Metering Skid — Zone vs Conduit
pins.anomaly_class: One flat OT VLAN spanning L0 process, L1 PLC, L2 HMI, and vendor laptop

red_quiz.prompt: IEC 62443 + 800-82 language: a ZONE is ___ and a CONDUIT is ___.
choices: A VLAN number / a fiber color
A set of assets with the same security requirements / a documented allowed path between zones
The Purdue level number / the switch hostname
The safety system / the business network
red_quiz.teach: Purdue describes function levels. Zones are drawn by risk. A whole Purdue level is usually too fat to be one zone. Conduits are explicit, deny-by-default paths.

blue_quiz.prompt: Vendor laptop sits on the PLC VLAN. 800-82-shaped fix?
choices: Give the vendor domain admin so they are faster
Put vendor access in a dedicated conduit through L3.5 jump host, time-boxed, logged, least privilege; PLC zone stays closed
Disable logging so the audit is cleaner
Bridge L0 sensors onto the laptop
blue_quiz.teach: Remote/vendor access is a first-class conduit, not a courtesy VLAN.

pins.name: SIS / Compensating Control
pins.anomaly_class: Unpatchable L1 controller; proposed 'fix' is to expose it for remote patch

red_quiz.prompt: 800-82r3 when a controller cannot host the control itself?
choices: Connect it to the internet so Windows Update can reach it
Compensating control in the conduit: in-path authentication, least privilege, monitoring — safety function stays independent
Delete the safety instrumented system
Treat OT like a laptop and force weekly reboot
red_quiz.teach: r3 is explicit: OT has availability and safety constraints IT does not. Where the device cannot take the control, the architecture takes it.

blue_quiz.prompt: Impact overlay in the 800-53r5 OT annex is used to ___?
choices: Pick a video game difficulty
Tailor the 800-53 control baseline to low / moderate / high OT impact — including safety and process consequence
Replace IEC 62443 entirely
Authorize Dubai Marina flights
blue_quiz.teach: 800-82r3 ships an OT overlay on 800-53r5. High-impact OT (export metering, SIS-adjacent) is not scored like a brochure site.

pins.name: SUC Partition — ZCR Walk
pins.anomaly_class: SUC never partitioned; vendor laptop, SIS, and HMI share one trust domain

red_quiz.prompt: IEC 62443-3-2 ZCR 3 mandatory splits include which of these?
choices: Split only by building floor
Separate business from IACS, separate safety-related assets, separate temporarily connected devices, separate wireless
Merge SIS into the PLC VLAN for faster trip times
Put every asset in one SL-4 zone
red_quiz.teach: ZCR 3.2–3.5: business ≠ IACS, safety stays its own zone, transient devices and wireless do not inherit the process zone.

choices: Buy a firewall, then invent zone names
Define SUC and access points → initial risk → partition zones/conduits → detailed risk per zone → assign SL-T → document requirements (then 3-3 implements the SL)
Copy Purdue L0–L5 as five zones and stop
Set everything to SL-4 so assessment is skipped
blue_quiz.teach: Zones are born from risk assessment, not from switch-port convenience.

pins.name: SL-T Assignment
pins.anomaly_class: SIS zone given SL-1; enterprise BI given SL-4

choices: How expensive the switch is
Target Security Level the zone/conduit must achieve after risk assessment — SL-1 casual/accidental through SL-4 well-resourced targeted adversary
The Purdue level number
A CVSS score
red_quiz.teach: SL-C capability, SL-T target, SL-A achieved. Design to SL-T; measure SL-A after controls land.

blue_quiz.prompt: Two zones SL-2 and SL-3 share a conduit. What does the conduit inherit?
choices: The lower SL so traffic is easy
The stricter need of the higher-SL zone — write-down from low-integrity to high-integrity is a first-class risk
No SL; conduits are just cables
SL-4 automatically
blue_quiz.teach: Conduits inherit security requirements from the zones they connect. Mismatched SLs get a control in the conduit, not a flat trunk.

pins.name: 800-53r5 OT Overlay Review
pins.anomaly_class: Team applied unmodified enterprise 800-53 High baseline to an unpatchable L1 controller

red_quiz.prompt: Where does the official OT overlay live?
choices: A blog table of invented control IDs
NIST SP 800-82r3 Appendix F — partial tailoring of 800-53 Rev. 5 and 800-53B Low/Moderate/High plus OT Discussion
IEC 62443-3-3 only
GCAA CAR-UAR
red_quiz.teach: Reference name: NIST SP 800-82 Rev 3 Operational Technology Overlay. The generated training plate is a schematic. Official IDs come from Appendix F.

blue_quiz.prompt: Controller cannot host SI-2 flaw remediation. 800-53 / 800-82 correct move?
choices: Mark the control NA and stop
Apply a compensating control under PL-11 that meets the intent in the conduit (monitor, restrict, broker) — not a waiver — and keep SIS independent
Force weekly OS patches on the safety PLC during loading
Drop the whole High baseline
blue_quiz.teach: 800-82r3: compensating controls are alternative safeguards that accomplish the intent. Availability and safety constrain how SI-2 / CM / AC land on live process.

kill_chain: SCAN — fly the pin, read the anomaly class label
TRACE — pick jamming vs spoof vs dark AIS vs legal no-fly vs OT zone-cross
EXPLOIT — in this range = unlock the quiz, not a live payload
REPORT — write the five-field KIN brief: Claim, Blast Radius, Root Cause class, Replayable Verification, Falsification

bosses.name: Crop Circle
bosses.win_condition: Blue restores a multi-sensor nav picture on the twin and files the interference report; Red has already classified it as spoof not jam.

bosses.name: Marina Night Clip
bosses.win_condition: Investigator packet complete: zone, 5 km HLS hit, night, registration gap, current safety-decision status.
